## Background
Today we are going to learn all about the **ggplot2** package in R.\
There are tons of graphics packages in R. These include "base R graphics" (like the `plot()` function we used last day) and add on packages like **ggplot2**.

### Comparing base graphics with ggplot
We can use the in-built data frame `cars` to play with plotting:

```{r}
head(cars,2) # default 6 lines

```
```{r}
plot(cars)
```

Now we try using ggplot:

First, we need to install the package with the `install.packages("")`command.

> This `install.packages("ggplot2")` only needs to be done ONCE. I don't need to run it in my quarto documents as it will result me re-instaling the package everytime I render my report...

Next, you need to load the package using `library()`.

> This needs to be done every time you want to use a function from a given package.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
#ggplot(cars) --> This only makes a blant canvas, but why? check below!
```

Every ggplot needs at least three layers:

1. **data** ("data": data.frame we want to plot from)
2. **aesthetics** ("aes": how the columns of the data map to the plot)
3. **geometry** ("geom_": how you want the plot drawn, points, lines, etc)

```{r}
# geom_smooth(): lm = linear fit, se = standard error and its default is TRUE
ggplot(data=cars) + aes(x=speed, y=dist) + geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method="lm",se=TRUE,color="blue") + 
  theme_bw() + 
  labs(x="Speed in (MPH)",
       y="Stopping Distance (ft)",
       title="Silly Plot of Stopping Distances")
```


## Gene Expression Plot

> Adding more plot aesthetics through aes()

```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```

```{r}

# No need to write (data=genes)
# No need to specify (x=,y=) because these are the default arguments
ggplot(genes) + aes(Condition1, Condition2) + geom_point()

```

> Question#1: How many genes are in this dataset?

```{r}

nrow(genes)

```

> Question#2: How many are "upregulated"?

```{r}

# head(genes) # Take a look at the dataset again
# genes$State # Print the state column out
table(genes$State)

```

```{r}

# genes$State == "up" # Returning logicals
sum(genes$State=="up")

```

> Question#3: What percentage of genes are "downregulated"?

```{r}

n.total <- nrow(genes)
n.down <- sum(genes$State=="down")
percentage_down = round(n.down/n.total*100, 2)

```

The percentage of downregulated genes is `r percentage_down`%, cool.


```{r}
# If we assign the plot to the value p, we can add features later, but note that these features can be also included when writing ggplot...

# Color my plot by state
p <-  ggplot(genes) + 
  aes(Condition1, Condition2, col=State) + 
  geom_point() + 
  theme_bw()

# Manually changing the colors
p <- p + scale_colour_manual( values=c("blue","gray","red") )

# Add a label layer
p <- p + labs(x="Control (no drug)",
              y= "Drug treated",
              title="Gene Expression Changes Upon Drug Treatment",
              subtitle="GLP-1 inhibitor from Novo")

# Load the plot
p
```

We can install extra package with `install.packages("patchwork") like the packages for spongebob colors or actually useful ones like **patchwork** for combining plots:

> `install.packages("patchwork")` note that this only to be done once.

```{r}
library(patchwork)

# Setup some example plots 
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp))
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear))
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_smooth(aes(disp, qsec))
p4 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_bar(aes(carb))

# Use patchwork to combine them here:
# (p1 | p2)/
# (p3 | p4)
(p1 | p2 | p3) /
      p4

```


```{r}

# Split it based on different States multi-panels
p + facet_wrap(~State)

```

## The Gapminder dataset

The gapminder dataset is rather famous and has lots of stuff we can plot ;-)
```{r}
# File location online
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"
gapminder <- read.delim(url)
```

Have a wee peak:
```{r}
head(gapminder)
```

> Question#1: How many data entries are there in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(gapminder)
```

> Question#2: How many countries are in this dataset?

```{r}
length(unique(gapminder$country))
```


```{r}
plot <- ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(gdpPercap, lifeExp, col=continent) + 
  geom_point(alpha=0.5) # alpha = dot transparency

plot
```

Break out a facet per continent
```{r}

plot + facet_wrap(~continent)

```


Histograms
```{r}
plot_hist <- ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent) +
  geom_histogram()

plot_hist

```

Bloxplot
```{r}
plot_box <- ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, continent, fill=continent) +
  geom_boxplot()

plot_box
```
